items.title: Current walking progress and recommended hardware for a new build
items.body:
Hi! Thank you for sharing the Microduck reconstruction, CAD and build logs.

I’m based in Bengaluru, India, and want to build a walking, talking replica. I saw your September 13 update showing the assembled HD-1910 version. Before ordering parts, could you help clarify:

1. Has it successfully stood or walked yet? Is there a recent video?
2. Has the `imu_to_dxl` board been tested, and is working firmware available?
3. For the quickest working build, would you recommend original Dynamixel XL330 motors or your HD-1910 version? Is a tested walking policy available for either replica configuration?
4. Are you or other community members offering tested boards, complete hardware kits, or assembled units?

My priority is getting a working prototype quickly. I’d be happy to share build results and fixes back with the project. Thanks!

items.title: 飞特版跟进请教：打印材料/质量、训练策略、HAT 板 PCBA、舵机参数 4 个问题
items.body:
你好！我在按你的飞特 HD-1910 版做复刻，目标是做一只能走路 + 有视觉/语音对话 + 接云端 LLM 的鸭子。
读了 microduck-replica 和 CAD 仓的文档，受益匪浅，有 4 个问题想请教（按我的下单优先级排序）。

## ① 打印材料与整机质量（最急，我要找打印服务下单）

你在 `imu-fix-1015` 里写「整鸭带电池 **806 g**，训练用 820 g，差 1.7%」。
我算了一下：官方 737.2 g + 15 只舵机各重 4.5 g ≈ 804.7 g，对得上。
我想让整机质量尽量贴近你那台，以便直接复用你的实机数据，所以想确认这个 806 g 的构成：

1. **是全 PLA，还是部分件用了铝合金增强？**
   CAD 仓 BOM 里「颈部 / 躯干底座 / 上腿加固板」标注了「可换铝合金增强」——
   你实际打的是塑料还是铝？
2. **填充率（infill）是多少？** 这在 Bambu Studio 的 3MF 里有预设，
   我要找打印服务商打（他们只收 STL，拿不到 3MF 参数），需要知道具体数值。
3. 层高 0.2 / 0.4 喷嘴 / PLA Basic 这几个参数，确认一下我没理解错。

另外：你的 3MF 是 09-15 版，v2.1 改了 TPU 合体轮胎。
**我们这种不做轮滑的版本，是不是直接按 09-15 那 52 个对象打就行？**

## ② 走路策略：重训还是调参

看到你 10-15 的记录里**收回了「舵机不行，要重训」**这个结论，
说「大家好多用他的跑通了」，元凶是 IMU 姿态模式（chip → gyro）。想确认现在的判断：

1. **现成 kissqy V167 策略 + 飞特舵机，是不是直接能走？** 还是要改动作缩放/滤波？
   （你的记录里用了「动作缩放 0.9、头滤波 0.5、腿滤波 0.7」）
2. **你 `software/training/` 里的 `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck-HD1910`，
   打算自己跑完整训练吗？** README 写「尚无本机实测通过的走路策略」
   「本次没有提交付费云端任务」。如果暂时不打算跑，我用 `--hf-jobs` 跑一版
   （官方说约 1–2 h / 十几元），训出来会发布回来给你。
3. 你提到「现有 Microduck 质量惯量仍是原版仿真值，后续需要按飞特实机数据校正」——
   **这个校正做了吗？** 还是仍用原版值？

## ③ HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板

看到 issue #25 有人问过套件，当时回答「舵机还没到」。现在应该到了，想再问一下：

1. **HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板有打样好的余量可转让吗？** 或者有没有拼单渠道？
   我们自己打样 4 层板 + SMT（113 个贴装位置、含 0603）起订量不划算。
2. 如果买不到，**嘉立创 PCBA 的 SMT 你走过吗？** 有没有踩过坑
   （哪些料要自己备、钢网要不要开）？

## ④ 舵机参数核对

你们和 LuwuDynamics 都用 `1910_m6.json`（`STS3215Actuator`）给 HD-1910 建模。想确认：

1. **HD-1910-C001 是否等同 HLS1910 / STS3215？** 飞特型号命名有点乱，
   XGO-Duck README 写 "HLS1910"，参数文件里写 `sts3215`。
   如果确认同族，我就直接沿用 `1910_m6.json`；否则要做系统辨识。
2. **规格书上的 10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的？** `1910_m6.json` 里的 `kt` 隐含电压假设，
   我们总线是 6.6–8.2 V（满电 8.4 V），想核对匹配。
3. 减速比、编码器分辨率、回差这三项规格书上没有 —— **你们实测过吗？**

（注：你文档里说「参数不是本项目自行辨识的结果」，所以这条也许没人答得上来 ——
那我就直接沿用并做实机对照。）

---

另外提一下我的扩展方向，如果你也在做可以一起搞：
除了走路，我还要加**视觉 + 语音对话 + 云端 LLM**（大致是 Reachy Mini conversation app 那套）。
有两个硬件问题想请教：

1. **HAT 上麦克风和喇叭的间距，自播报时的回声（AEC）好消吗？**
   我想做声纹识别主人/家人，如果 AEC 做不好声纹就废了。
2. 摄像头装在头里，**你那边出图正常吗？** 官方代码 `--rotate` 默认 90，
   你记录里写「摄像头调整排线后在官方 B1 下出图」—— 是转 90 还是 180？

非常感谢！有问题我也会把结果反馈回来。

items.title: 复刻前确认：成功样机的身体IMU、供电、软件版本及完整装配指南
items.body:
你好，感谢整理和分享制作资料。我是硬件初学者，计划按 XL330 路线做个人复刻，目前尚未采购整机或通电，想在购买前确认资料能覆盖到哪一步。

我已下载 `maker-20260916` 的四个 ZIP，并按仓库 manifest 核对 SHA-256。制作包中的 README 和 `01_物料清单.md` 说明：包内不含产品运行时、独立 IMU 和旧整机供电方案，完成后的新供电/身体姿态方案也尚未提供。仓库同时展示了成功复刻的样机，所以想请教这台样机实际使用的配套资料：

1. **身体 IMU**：成功样机使用哪块板、哪版固件、什么安装方向？它是否兼容当前官方 `robotd` 的 `imu_to_dxl v2`（LSM6DSV16X、ID 200、地址124）？若需另购或自行制造，是否有对应入口？
2. **供电**：样机15台 XL330 的实际供电范围是什么？是否有在 ROBOTIS 标称3.7–6.0V范围内验证过站立、行走的接法及配套策略？公开包已提醒不能直接2S供电，因此不敢照旧接线图上电。
3. **软件配套**：能否提供与演示样机对应的系统镜像，或主控系统版本、运行仓库/commit、配置、IMU固件、ONNX模型版本清单？我已验证官方 `alpha_walking.onnx` 能加载和做合成输入推理，但还没有任何真机验证。
4. **装配说明**：[这篇复刻文章](https://wuwei.me/2026/10/11/microduck/)提到《Microduck复刻装配指南》。该指南是否另有公开入口？我在已下载包中没有找到包含逐位置紧固件、线束针序和完整接线的指南本体。如当前仍有需要自行设计/验证的部分，列明范围也很有帮助。

我的目标是先确认一套与成功样机一致、可以实际采购/制造和部署的组合，再进入单件试印、台架检查和整机装配。若上述部分暂未公开或尚未验证，直接说明即可，方便初学者判断何时适合开工。谢谢！

items.title: MicroDuck Feetech Replica – Hardware, Firmware and Software Clarification Before Assembly
items.body:
Hello,

My name is Gianluca, and I am building your MicroDuck Replica using the Feetech 3D-printing project (52 printed parts). I have already started printing the components.

Thank you for sharing your work and documenting your progress. I would like to reproduce your Feetech version as faithfully as possible.

Before purchasing the electronics and assembling the robot, I would appreciate your help confirming the current hardware and software configuration. I have read your repository and recent updates, but I want to make sure I follow the latest tested setup rather than an earlier design or a component that is still under development.

I hope to clarify the remaining questions in one message and avoid disturbing you repeatedly during the build.

1. Recommended hardware and electronics

Could you please confirm the exact hardware configuration you currently recommend for a new Feetech build?

Are 15 Feetech HD-1910-C001 servos still the correct model and quantity?

Is the Radxa Zero 3W still the recommended main computer? Is the 8 GB RAM / 64 GB eMMC variant compatible with your design and software?

Which controller boards, adapters and custom PCBs are required for the completed robot?

Which components have already been tested on your assembled Feetech robot, and which are still experimental or planned?

Is there an updated bill of materials (BOM) that reflects your current build?

2. Servo interface, connections and calibration

I understand that you successfully controlled all 15 Feetech servos using a Feetech URT-2 USB adapter.

Is the URT-2 also the recommended interface between the Radxa and the servo bus in the completed robot, or is it mainly used for testing and calibration?

How should the 15 servos be physically connected and powered?

Is a specific bus distribution board, adapter or wiring arrangement required?

Which wiring diagram and power-connection instructions should I follow?

Where can I find the latest servo ID mapping, joint directions, zero positions, standing positions and safe movement limits?

3. IMU and orientation feedback

I have read about the imu_to_dxl board and the recent firmware contribution by @Abo1ish. I understand that an initial firmware implementation has been tested and that IMU orientation can be displayed in the servo-web diagnostic interface through J-Link.

I also understand that the Feetech 15-byte bus protocol has not yet been implemented in that firmware.

Could you please clarify:

Which IMU hardware is installed in your current Feetech robot?

Which IMU solution do you recommend for a new Feetech build?

Is the imu_to_dxl board ready to build and use, or should I wait for a newer hardware or firmware revision?

Is the alternative BNO085 IMU connected directly to the Radxa still a recommended option?

Has either solution already been integrated and tested with the Feetech movement-control software, rather than only with the diagnostic interface?

Where can I find the current wiring instructions, firmware, software configuration and calibration procedure for the recommended IMU?

My aim is to install an IMU that the movement-control software can actually use.

4. Current movement software and capabilities

I have seen your video showing the Feetech robot standing up and sitting down. I have also read about your FeetechIo implementation and the current status of walking-policy training.

Could you please confirm which of the following capabilities have already been physically tested on your Feetech version?

Standing up and sitting down

Maintaining balance using IMU feedback

Walking forward

Turning while walking

Recovering after a disturbance or fall

Is the feetech branch of your MicroDuck fork currently ready to run on an assembled Radxa-based robot, or should a new builder initially use only the servo-web diagnostic console?

Does the Feetech version require a separately trained walking policy? If so, are the required model files already available, or is this work still in progress?

5. Operating system and first startup

I noticed your recent Radxa Zero 3W Armbian release and the documentation about boot issues on certain board revisions.

Which operating-system image and installation procedure do you currently recommend?

Are there any Radxa board revisions that require special attention?

Which instructions should I follow for initial servo configuration and calibration?

Is there a recommended first-start and testing procedure before enabling full-body movements?

6. Power supply and battery

For the initial build, I would like to follow the power configuration used in your working Feetech robot.

Could you please confirm:

The battery model, voltage, capacity and connector you currently use

The recommended power connection for the 15 Feetech servos

How the Radxa receives its regulated 5 V supply

Any required voltage regulators, distribution boards, switches or protection components

The correct power-on and power-off sequence

If available, could you please point me to your latest corrected wiring diagram?

7. Camera, distance sensor and audio

Could you please confirm the exact camera, distance sensor, microphone, speaker and audio interface or amplifier recommended for the current Feetech build?

I noticed that your recent documentation recommends the VL53L5CX instead of the VL53L8CX because of the mounting-hole dimensions of face_part. Is the VL53L5CX the correct choice for the Feetech printed parts?

Is the beak servo already independently controllable through the available software? If so, where can I find the corresponding command or documentation?

8. Current documentation and remaining work

Your project is progressing quickly, and I want to make sure I am using the latest instructions.

Could you please point me to the current recommended BOM, wiring diagram, firmware, software branch and assembly instructions for the Feetech version?

It would also be helpful to know which components or software features are still under development and should not yet be considered ready for a new build.

If these questions are already answered in your latest documentation, links to the relevant files would be more than sufficient.

Thank you very much for your time and for sharing your project. I appreciate any guidance you can provide to help me assemble and configure the Feetech MicroDuck correctly.

Best regards, Gianluca

items.title: [task] imu-to-dxl v0.3 firmware P0 fixes + rebuild
items.body:
## Type
`task`

## Goal
基于 v0.3 硬件真源修复 `imu_to_dxl` 固件的启动、SFLP 与 DXL 通信缺陷，重新生成可追溯 ELF/BIN，并完成单板 U2D2 烧录验收。

本任务是 #7 零回包台架任务的固件实现单；#7 保留为实板联调/波形验收。

## Confirmed root causes / defects
1. `SPI1_CR2` 仅设置 8-bit DS，未设置 `FRXTH=1`；首个 8-bit SPI 接收可能永久等待 `RXNE`，发生在 DXL 主循环之前，可直接解释首包 RX=0 B。
2. LSM6DSV16X SFLP/FIFO 配置值不正确：game rotation FIFO enable、SFLP ODR 固定位、game init 位。
3. FIFO tag 位于 bit7:3，当前解码方向错误。
4. USART2 RX 在发送期间常开，PA3 与 U6-Y/DXL_DATA 同网；Status 自回听且未清 `RDR/ORE`，会破坏后续请求。
5. SPI/USART 等待无超时；Protocol 2.0 TX/RX 缺 byte stuffing；Read/Write 长度边界不足。

## Non-negotiable contracts
- 硬件：v0.3 · STM32G031F8P6 · LSM6DSV16X · SN74LVC1G125，OE# `PA1`，低电平发送。
- DXL：Protocol 2.0 · ID `200` · `1 Mbps`。
- 主机数据：addr `124` · `12 B`；gyro `i16 LE ×3` + quaternion xyz `IEEE half LE`。
- 保留 #6 的 `GPIOA_BASE = 0x50000000` 修复。
- 以 ST 官方 LSM6DSV16X driver/datasheet/AN5763 与 STM32G031 RM0444 为寄存器依据，不凭同系列芯片猜值。

## Required implementation
### Phase A — restore DXL lifeline
- [ ] SPI 8-bit RX 阈值配置正确，并为 SPI/USART 所有轮询等待增加有界超时。
- [ ] IMU WHO_AM_I/init 失败不得阻塞 DXL 主循环；诊断表能区分 `DXL alive / IMU failed`。
- [ ] 处理 TX 自回听：发送期间禁用 RE，或发送后可靠 drain RDR 并清 ORE/FE/NE；给出选择依据。
- [ ] 标准 Ping Status（Model Number + Firmware Version）与普通 Read 可用。

### Phase B — restore IMU/SFLP data
- [ ] 修正 SFLP game rotation FIFO enable、ODR、INIT 与寄存器写后 readback。
- [ ] FIFO tag 按 `(tag_byte >> 3) & 0x1F` 解码并识别 game rotation tag。
- [ ] addr124 的 gyro/quaternion 非固定零，姿态变化方向合理。

### Phase C — protocol robustness
- [ ] Protocol 2.0 TX stuffing / RX unstuffing，Length 与 CRC 基于线上的 stuffed packet 正确计算。
- [ ] Read/Write/Status 缓冲区全部有硬边界，越界请求返回明确错误，不静默截断/越界写。
- [ ] 增加 `sync_read(0x82)`、stuffing、自回听/ORE、超长读写的 host tests。
- [ ] 评估并解决 1 Mbps 下 SPI drain 阻塞 UART 的风险（RX IRQ + ring buffer，或有测量依据的等效方案）。

## Deliverables
- 固件源码：`imu_to_dxl/firmware/`
- 构建产物：`firmware/build/imu_to_dxl.elf`、`.bin`（产物可不入 Git，但 Issue 必须记录 commit/hash/size）
- 测试记录：本 Issue 评论；涉及规格变更时更新对应 wiki/docs

## Acceptance
- [ ] `make clean && make host-test && make g031` 全部 exit 0。
- [ ] 记录 commit、ELF/BIN SHA-256 与 `arm-none-eabi-size`。
- [ ] SWD/隔离验证证明启动不再停在 SPI RXNE 等待。
- [ ] 单挂 ID200：连续 Ping 与 Read(124,12) 各 1000 次，无丢包/CRC 错。
- [ ] `duck-control` 同路径 Sync Read（ID200 为首设备）连续运行 10 min，无 timeout/ShortRead。
- [ ] @136 诊断能区分 IMU present/SFLP live；quat 达到 ready 并随姿态变化。
- [ ] 含 `FF FF FD` 的 12 B 载荷通过 stuffing 抓包/主机解码测试。
- [ ] 结果回写 Issue，完成后加 `ready-for-pm`，由 pm 验收关闭。

## assignee-agent
`software`（固件/协议）；`hardware` 仅在 #7 配合烧录、波形和供电台架；`pm` 验收。

## References
- #6 GPIOA base 修复
- #7 v0.3 U2D2 zero-reply bring-up
- `imu_to_dxl/docs/hardware.md`
- `imu_to_dxl/docs/protocol.md`
- `wiki/concepts/imu-to-dxl-firmware-build.md`

items.title: control: the bus reads with fast sync read
items.body:
Sixteen devices answering a sync read send sixteen status packets, each with its own ten-byte
protocol 2.0 header and each preceded by that device's bus turnaround. Fast sync read
(instruction 0x8A) asks the same question — the instruction packet is a plain sync read's — and
takes one packet back: every device appends its block to a single status packet from the
broadcast id.

rustypot 1.7.0 added it, and `with_fast_sync_read()` on the controller routes every
`sync_read_*` through it. So the tick's combined IMU+servo read, the once-a-second voltage and
temperature read, and the startup position read all use it without any of them naming it — one
decision at `open_controller`, and nothing at the call sites.

This is the same cost `return_delay_time = 0` is pinned for. The register check stays: every
other transaction on this bus — the register reads and writes, the pings, the gains, torque
enable — is an ordinary one that still pays a turnaround per device.

## `bus.fast_sync_read`, on by default

Whether the instruction works is a property of **firmware**, and that is the one thing on this
bus the daemon cannot talk its way out of:

- **XL330 firmware v46 or newer.**
- **The `imu_to_dxl` v2 board implements 0x8A.** It is `id 200` and the first block of the
  tick's read, so this one is not optional.

So it is a key in `[bus]` rather than a constant, reachable from `robotctl configure` beside
`bus.port`, needing a `robotd` restart like the rest of that section. A board built before the
firmware needs one setting, once, and off it behaves exactly as it did before this branch —
`open_bus` says so once in the journal, because a robot running the slow path is otherwise
indistinguishable from a slow robot.

**The default is on, because getting it wrong is unambiguous rather than subtle.** A device that
does not implement 0x8A does not answer at all, so *every* read times out — not some of them
returning something plausible. Bus drops from the first tick, `min_achieved_hz` sees an unhealthy
robot, and a release that turned this on against firmware that cannot do it rolls itself back.

Nothing probes for support at startup: a device that does not answer looks exactly like one that
is unpowered, and a probe would have to tell those two apart before it could say anything useful.

It is not a *feature switch* in the registry, though it is a `Bool` — the editor's front page is
"what does this robot do", and this is "what does this robot's firmware understand", which
belongs beside the serial port.

## Not run on a robot

Nothing answered the scan from here, so this has not been near hardware.
`cargo run --example fast_sync_read_bench` in rustypot checks both instructions return the same
data and times them side by side, which is the cheapest way to settle it on `olducky` — and
`bus.fast_sync_read = false` is the answer if the `imu_to_dxl` board turns out not to implement
the instruction.

## Note on byte stuffing

rustypot does not de-stuff a fast sync read's body — it walks it with a fixed stride, as the
vendor SDK does (`GroupFastSyncRead::rxPacket` passes `skip_stuffing = true`). It checks every
block's CRC, so a stuffed byte surfaces as a checksum error rather than as shifted data. Worth
naming because de-stuffing is exactly why `1.6.0` was the previous floor here: a present current
of `-1` puts `FF FF` in the payload, and `FF FF FD` is what triggers stuffing. If that shows up
on hardware it will look like occasional dropped reads, not wrong numbers.

## Tested

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (one
pre-existing warning in `chorale.rs`, untouched here), `cargo test -p duck-control -p
robotd-params -p robotctl` — clean. Not run on a robot.

items.title: 支持 Dynamixel 2.0 FAST_SYNC_READ (0x8A)
items.body:
你好，感谢开源这个项目。
想提一个和当前 Pollen 官方 microduck 主线兼容性有关的功能请求：为 imu_to_dxl 固件增加 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 的 FAST_SYNC_READ (0x8A) 支持。
背景：
- 当前官方 microduck 的总线实现默认启用 Fast Sync Read，普通 sync_read 会走 0x8A：
  - [https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/duck-control/src/bus.rs](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/duck-control/src/bus.rs?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
  - [https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/docs/design/robotd-design.md](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck/blob/main/docs/design/robotd-design.md?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- 官方默认配置里 bus.fast_sync_read 为 true；若某个设备不支持 0x8A，整组读取会超时。
- 本项目当前已经实现普通 SYNC_READ (0x82)，并且 ID=200 / addr=124 / len=12 的 DXL 数据布局与官方要求是对齐的，但目前 board.h / dxl2.c 中还没有看到 0x8A 的处理。
希望可以考虑：
1. 增加 DXL_INST_FAST_SYNC_READ = 0x8A。
2. 按 Dynamixel 2.0 Fast Sync Read 规范处理 ID 列表、设备顺序和聚合响应。
3. 保持现有 IMU 数据映射：ID 200、地址 124、长度 12。
4. 如果方便，增加一个和当前官方 robotd / rustypot 对拍的测试，最好能验证 IMU 与 XL330 同总线时的 0x8A 读取。
这项支持对 XL330 原版路线会很有价值，可以避免为了兼容 IMU 而在 robotd.toml 中关闭 fast_sync_read。

items.title: 将 J-Link IMU 姿态并入 servo-web，固件归入硬件目录
items.body:
现有 `software/servo-web/` 增加可选的 J-Link IMU 数据源：同一个 3D 鸭子以舵机回读驱动关节角、以 IMU 四元数驱动躯干姿态。未启用 IMU 时隐藏该区域，原有调试功能照常。

## 实现

- `python server.py --port COM5 --imu-jlink imu-jlink.json`：一个服务、原 `/ws` 追加 `type: imu` 消息，现有日志文件新增 IMU 分类。
- `--fake --imu-jlink ...` 可只接裸板；`--fake --imu-demo` 可完全无硬件检查。两种数据源在界面分别标记。
- 保留默认绕 Y +90° 安装方向、显示归零及原始姿态；断流/过期保留末帧并撤销实时状态，关节变换保持独立。重心显示标明为模型几何估计。
- 固件与 Keil 工程放在 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`。只保留一个预编译 HEX；解码后固定 SHA 绑定已审核的 RAM 布局，连接后仍逐字节核对实板 Flash，无需仓库中的 BIN/MAP。
- 复用原模型、build_model.py、CDN 和现有硬件 PDF；不包含独立查看器、CMD 启动入口或 ZIP 打包脚本。
- 驱动及许可证保留。硬件说明按现有原理图校正 J3：SWD 使用1/2/3/6，第4/5脚为 UART_RX/TX，第6脚为 VTref。

## 验证

- `python selftest.py`：全部通过。
- `python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py test_imu_server.py`：45 passed、59 subtests passed。
- `node --test test_imu_attitude.cjs`：13项全部通过。
- 迁移后 `Tools/test.ps1`：协议106项、IMU16场景、寄存器14项、Python4项全部通过；固件 Core/Drivers/Startup/Keil 和 HEX 未改逻辑或重新构建。
- 浏览器联合演示：模拟30号关节目标2048→2300、实际回读2297时，IMU躯干仍持续更新；归零、安装方向、原始姿态、IMU日志、断流显示均通过。以不带IMU参数重启后面板隐藏、15/15模拟舵机在线，原滑块仍可用。

## 范围

此次不连接真板或真舵机；尚未验证两者同时运行及现场轴向。原开发板此前验证过 J-Link 约20Hz读取，SDK建连可能重启板上程序。真实模式要求填写自己的DLL和探针序列号，`resume` 默认false，只有显式启用且固件验证通过后才能恢复暂停CPU。

**固件仍是早期 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 / ID200 / 地址124的12字节基线，飞特地址56、15字节协议及 `imu200.py check` 留到下一步。** 姿态页面不测平移、不判断真实接触或整机平衡。详细记录见 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/VALIDATION.md`。

items.title: Add Pollen's Arena reference policies, a fuller twin and seven more
items.body:
Sweep of 2026-09-25 → 2026-09-28. **198 → 207 entries.** (Counts from here on exclude the 14 table-of-contents lines; earlier PRs included them, so the list was 198, not 212.)

## Official: the Microduck Arena

Pollen published baselines for a challenge series it calls the **Microduck Arena**: a 2 m sprint, a 2 m roller sprint and a 1.5 m hill climb. Each was trained unchanged from its challenge recipe (4096 envs, 3000 iterations, seed 1), with the commit and command to reproduce it recorded on its card.

The three policies are public on the Hub. The repo they cite, `pollen-robotics/microduck-challenges`, returns **404**, so the entry says the challenge repository isn't public yet rather than linking it.

**Three "arenas", disambiguated:**
- **Arena reference policies**: Pollen's official Arena baselines
- **microduck-arena (3v3 football)**: `00make`'s community game, relabelled from the plain "Microduck Arena" so it can't be mistaken for Pollen's
- **Microduck walker arena**: `craigm26`'s new community tool, whose entry says outright that it isn't Pollen's Arena

## Added

| Section | Entry | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation | [microduck-twin](https://github.com/digows/microduck-twin) | **Completes** Pollen's twin rather than replacing it: voice, battery and thermals, the head microphone as a sensor, rollers, a console — around the real daemons, nothing retrained. Apache-2.0 |
| Simulation | [microduck_rl_mac](https://github.com/keeeeenw/microduck_rl_mac) | Official tasks, rewards, randomisation and BAM model intact on Apple Silicon (CPU physics + Apple GPU PPO); walking demonstrated on M1 Max |
| Policies | [MicroDuck Piano Learning](https://github.com/KhushiJ2911/microduck-piano-learning) | Two ducks on a floor keyboard; states plainly that 1 of 64 worlds passed every gate and it isn't yet a score-following performance |
| Agent Tools | [Laya Vision find-and-kick](https://huggingface.co/thaitea/laya-vision-microduck-kick) | 201M VLM drives the duck from its head camera, ~70 ms per decision; live demo Space. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 |
| Apps | [Microduck walker arena](https://huggingface.co/spaces/craigm26/microduck-arena) | Every walker on one field, identical worlds, only the network differs |
| Apps | [duck3d](https://github.com/guang384/duck3d) | Native wgpu desktop console, same ONNX Runtime version as `robotd` |
| Apps | [ArduPilot Neural Mixer](https://github.com/virtualrobotix/Ardupilot-Neural-Mixer) | Walking policy **inside ArduPilot firmware** as plain C. SITL walks; stood 15 s as HIL on a Pixhawk 6C; real robot still needs a servo backend — tagged sim-only |
| Hardware | [microduck-community-kit](https://github.com/jyg9/microduck-community-kit) | `imu_to_dxl` board + firmware + host tests, battery board, servo hub, Feetech debugger. Apache-2.0 |

## Double caught and skipped

**`virtualrobotix/microduck-replica`** isn't marked as a fork, but its readme reproduces `fanhao375/microduck-replica` (already listed), down to first-person lines such as *"open an issue and I will post a fresh one"* that point at fanhao375's own issues. It's a duplicate of an existing entry.

## Also skipped

- `mshooter/microduck_academy` — a JdeRobot Robotics Academy server, still under construction (the server itself is unchecked). Worth revisiting
- `Will10005914/microduck-jump-videos`, `SIJEYUSES/MicroDuck-Agent` — too thin
- `PierreRouanet/*`, `wangmeng111/*` — no description
- `kathula29/bird-robot`, `hellobs/learned-duck` — different robots or homages
- Study repos with no description

## Checks

Tests 6/6 · `policies.json` regenerated and valid · revocations clean · `awesome-lint` clean · all new URLs 200.

items.title: Read the beta's head IMU (LSM6DSV16X) in robotd, on by default there
items.body:
The beta board's head IMU is an **LSM6DSV16X** on the face board's own I²C bus (`/dev/i2c-3`, `0x6a`), the same chip as the body IMU on the power board. This reads it, in robotd, on by default on a beta. **The zero3 is unchanged**: tofd still reads its BMI088, and it stays off by default.

### Why robotd, and why it can be on

The head IMU lived in tofd only because the zero3's BMI088 shares the HAT's I²C bus with the ToF. On the beta the ToF is on SPI and the IMU has its own bus. robotd already owns the kinematics that place the IMU (`frames.head_imu`).

The BMI088 cost ~4 % of a core at 100 Hz, almost all of it I²C transactions (two per sample; `docs/project/tof-on-demand.md`). This chip fuses the orientation itself (SFLP game vector) and batches gyro, accel and quaternion into its FIFO. robotd wakes 15 times a second and reads everything queued in **one burst**: two transactions for ~4 samples, and no fusion on the CPU. It runs at **60 Hz**: the body IMU runs at the control loop's 50 Hz, and the SFLP's nearest rate is 60.

### What changes

- **`robotd/src/head_imu.rs`**: the bring-up ported from `imu_to_dxl` (reset, reload the factory trimming, configure, verify, which is the fw 6 "drunk robot" fix), the FIFO decoder, and the reader thread. It uses raw `/dev/i2c-N` through `libc`, so there are no new crates and the Yocto crate list is unaffected.
- robotd serves **`head_imu.stream`** on `/run/robotd.sock`, in the same `HeadImuFrame` shape tofd serves on a zero3.
- **`[head_imu] enabled`** is now optional: unset means the board decides (zero3 off, beta on), and an explicit value wins on both. `robotctl configure` restarts whichever daemon reads it.
- Asking the wrong daemon (tofd on a beta, robotd on a zero3) gets an accepted answer whose `unavailable` names the right one.
- Docs: the config template, the cheatsheet, `tof-on-demand.md`, and the protocol's frame docs.

### Verified on a beta board

Installed with `scripts/dev-push.sh` through the normal health gate.

- robotd logs `head IMU found: LSM6DSV16X, fused on the chip at="/dev/i2c-3 0x6a"`; tofd logs `the head IMU on this board is robotd's`.
- Subscribed from a client: 58.1 frames/s at 60 Hz (the chip's clock runs ~3 % slow), no `seq` gaps, |accel| = 9.93 m/s² at rest, gyro ≈ 0, unit quaternions, increasing timestamps.
- **CPU: ~0.9 % of one core** for the `head-imu` thread at 60 Hz (60 s, no subscriber; ~1.5 % at 120 Hz), against the BMI088's ~4 % at 100 Hz.
- Before writing the decoder, I checked on the chip with `i2ctransfer` that one read from `FIFO_DATA_OUT_TAG` returns consecutive records (the address wraps 0x7E → 0x78).
- `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` and the tests of every touched crate pass. 8 new tests decode records taken from the board.

### IMU mounting on the beta (confirmed on hardware)

Both IMUs now report in robot axes (`x` forward, `y` left, `z` up) on a beta. Each was checked by tilting the robot or head and watching the readout.

- **Body IMU:** the beta's power board lies flat, so its mount is the identity (`SflpDecoder::BETA_MOUNT`). robotd picks the mount by `[board] version` through `DynamixelIo::set_imu_mount`; the zero3 keeps `DEFAULT_MOUNT` (+90° about Y). Checked in `robotctl monitor`.
- **Head IMU:** frames are in head axes: head = `[−z, −x, +y]` of the chip's (+90° about X, then −90° about Z). Pitch, roll and yaw checked with the new command below.
- **`robotctl head-imu`:** a live one-line readout of the head's roll, pitch and yaw, where it measures up, and the gyro.

### Open

- **`frames.head_imu` is still the zero3 HAT's mount.** On a beta the frames are already in head axes, so the right pose there is the head link's own (identity rotation), not the HAT's. The model needs that per-board case; the field's doc says so.
- No `API_VERSION` bump: robotd answering a method it used to refuse is additive. Flag it if the reviewer reads that differently.

items.title: docs: add simulation-first reverse-engineering guides and parameter maps
items.body:
## Summary

Deepens the public Microduck reverse-engineering documentation while making the project substantially easier to enter for non-expert readers.

### New paired English / Simplified Chinese guides

- beginner-friendly **Start Here** project map
- **Simulation First** quickstart using official MJCF models and existing official ONNX policies before hardware work
- staged **Public Reproduction Roadmap** from simulation to small hardware benches, mechanical subassemblies and sim-to-real validation
- detailed **Hardware Parameter Reference**
- **Structure and Assembly Map** that turns the MJCF/mesh tree into understandable robot modules
- detailed **Sim-to-Real Parameter Reference** covering BAM, voltage, sag, delay, backlash, domain randomization, contact and terrain

### Navigation / information architecture

Reworks both repository home pages and both documentation indexes so a new reader can choose a goal-oriented path instead of encountering a flat list of technical pages. Updates both roadmaps accordingly.

### Examples of newly documented public parameters

- 15 physical motor IDs / 14 policy joints / 61-D observations / 50 Hz
- exact current runtime motor IDs and home pose
- current simulation joint limits and rigid-body inertial masses
- pinned full-collision model inertial-mass sum (~737.243 g)
- 1 Mbps bus, 20 ms tick, current EEPROM expectations and state conversions
- LSM6DSV16X / `imu_to_dxl` v2 data format and orientation handling
- official simulation-model mesh instance counts (clearly labeled as model instances, not production purchase quantities)
- BAM M6 configuration: `kp_fw=200`, 6.5–8.2 V, voltage sag, 3–6 lag steps
- ±1° backlash model per servo joint
- CoM, mass/inertia, friction, armature, IMU and encoder domain-randomization ranges
- rough-terrain dimensions and contact-softening values
- explicit documentation of the version-sensitive runtime/training low-pass-filter difference

### Public-source boundary

All additions are based on public official sources or clearly labeled public community reconstruction. Simulation-model quantities are not presented as production BOM quantities. Unpublished PCB, wiring, manufacturing, fastener and production details remain unresolved rather than guessed.

### Upstream snapshot

- `pollen-robotics/microduck`: `590b986bd8c0d50ae02cb3ea2f59c463b6828168`
- `pollen-robotics/microduck_rl`: `d424a0c899f6b33cbd3daeb279913134349c0b63`
- `Rhoban/bam`: `620a64fe67c1afe94fca81da73b128c7aed17c5f`

items.title: Drop two dead entries, disambiguate the Isaac Lab ports, add six
items.body:
Daily sweep plus the requested duplicate/stale audit. 183 → 187 entries.

## Audit results

Checked all 155 GitHub and Hugging Face URLs for dead links and redirects, and cross-checked every entry for the same project appearing twice under different URLs, duplicate titles, and titles that collide once punctuation is ignored.

**No true duplicates.** No URL appears twice anywhere (`awesome-lint` already enforces that), and no project is listed twice under different URLs. `pollen-robotics/microduck` resolves 12 times, but that's the Official entry plus eleven deep links to individual docs — intended.

**Two dead entries, both removed:**
- **nottyduck** — `reachjalil/nottyduck` is 404 and the owner has no successor repo. Its Hub repo `reachjalil/nottyduck-policies` still resolves, but its own card says *"No policy artifact is published in the initial scaffold"* (2 files, untouched since 2026-08-29). The entry promised trained gesture policies, a 3D office mapper and a training CLI — none of it is fetchable. Removed rather than repointed at an empty scaffold.
- **MicroDuckSwarm** — `virtualmagician/MicroDuckSwarm` is 404. The owner's remaining repos (`SwarmUI`, a 2016 Zooids paper mirror; `StageWand`, stage-lighting hardware) are unrelated, so there's no rename to follow.

**One stale URL, fixed:** the Isaac Lab port link carried a branch path that GitHub was redirecting (`blob/5usu/microduck-port/…` → `blob/microduck-port/…`).

**Three Isaac Lab ports, two indistinguishable titles.** `isaaclab-microduck` (kabilankb) and `isaaclab_microduck` (dreamerarun) are genuinely different projects but read identically. Now labelled by physics backend — **(Newton)** and **(PhysX)** — so the three read as three.

## Added

| Section | Entry | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Simulation | [microduck_genesis](https://github.com/green-creeper/microduck_genesis) | Genesis World as a drop-in: a TCP `duck-body` server the **real daemons** attach to via `--sim`, plus keyboard policy rehearsal. Apache-2.0 |
| Simulation | [microduck_rl_tutorial](https://github.com/rocPAI-Forge/microduck_rl_tutorial) | ROCm teaching lab: fundamentals → smoke run → ~4 min train on MI300X → eval vs reference checkpoint → teleop. MIT |
| Policies | [microduck-standup](https://huggingface.co/QingMuLYL/microduck-standup) | Episodic get-up published against manifest schema 2 with its `robotctl policy add` line, training branch and commit; admits the export came from a dirty checkout |
| Agent Tools | [Harboria](https://github.com/Harboria/harboria) | Rust runtime for long-running assistants, duck as first adapter. Real code (48 files, domain model + daemon + CLI), marked early |
| Hardware | [Fanduck](https://github.com/7757/fanduck) | **A finished, photographed replica** — sourcing → printing → assembly, with BOM, print files, board files mirrored. Licence file pins the upstream commit and flags the official model as non-commercial |
| Hardware | [microduck_imu_to_ttl](https://github.com/avanx/microduck_imu_to_ttl) | Open-hardware `imu_to_dxl` board (LSM6DSV16X on the half-duplex Dynamixel bus). Fills a part replica projects keep listing as *still to be designed* |

## Skipped

- `KilllerBoss/microduck-kopfstand-apk` — Android APK bundling the policies, no license (same call as MicroDuckTrainer)
- `Nico-robot/*`, `cdeplanne/*` — "Published from the Microduck Arena", no description
- `alextechradar/awesome-microduck` — a **third** competing list (CC0, and it links to `joeynyc/microduck-mcp`). Still the maintainer's call, as with the other two
- Empty repos, and forks of the build tutorial with no changes described

## Checks

Tests 6/6 · `policies.json` regenerated (nottyduck removed from the registry too) and valid · revocations clean · `awesome-lint` clean · all new URLs 200.

items.title: docs: robotd-design is organised by subsystem, and draws the bus
items.body:
`robotd-design.md` was ordered by the two slices it was written for, so finding out how
anything works meant knowing which increment built it. The tick was described twice (§4.1
and §5.10), the two diagrams that orient a reader were inside §3.1, and the bring-up state
machine was a §5.7.1.

## The new order

Three tiers, so the important part is the part you land on:

- **§1 The shape of it** — the whole system on one screen: the bus and who owns the port,
  who talks to `robotd`, the crate boundary, the tick, and the five invariants, each
  pointing at the section that enforces it.
- **§2–§4** — reference detail in the order data moves: the bus layer and `RobotIo`,
  observations, the policy, safety, the model; then the API (intents in, state out,
  bring-up, health, maintenance); then what surrounds the loop (snapshots, params, `padd`).
- **§5–§9** — why it exists, the slices, testing, decisions, deferred, open.

No reasoning was dropped — it moved, and the duplicated tick became one section.

## Added

Nothing owned these, and `docs/README.md` says this page owns the bus:

- **The bus topology.** Sixteen devices on one UART — `/dev/ttyS2` at 1 Mbps, protocol v2,
  the `imu_to_dxl` board at id 200 first, then `20–24 / 30–34 / 10–14`.
- **Port ownership, and that nothing enforces it.** `serialport` sets `TIOCEXCL`, which only
  stops an unprivileged opener — `robotd.service` runs as root, so `robotd init` against a
  running daemon really does put two writers on one bus. `serial-getty@ttyS2` is the other
  claimant, masked by `setup-board.sh`, and `fuser -v /dev/ttyS2` is the command that
  answers "who has the bus".
- **The slow path.** Registers 144–146 once a second, on the same clock as the achieved-rate
  window, and why it cannot fold into the tick's read.

## Corrected against the code

| the page said | the code does |
|---|---|
| `MissedTickBehavior::Delay` | `Skip` — and the page now says why `Delay` is wrong here |
| `RobotIo` is two methods | six, plus two defaulted |
| walk-or-stand on `\|twist\|` | the priority chain: roulade > kick > ground pick > sit/rise > stand > walk |
| fall → limp is unconditional | the verdict is reported and gates nothing; limp-fall is what answers a fall, and it ships on |
| the wheeled configuration is dropped | it is a params preset, `policy.mode = "roller"` |
| tunables are in §8 | §8 was the testing section |

Also dropped two "open" items that were resolved in place, and the "not yet run on
hardware" note that `roadmap.md` already contradicts.

## Section numbers moved

Five call sites cite them and move with them: `duck-control/src/lib.rs`,
`robotd/src/params.rs` (×2), `deploy/robotd.toml`, `README.md`. `robotd/src/main.rs`'s
module doc gets rewritten rather than retargeted — it claimed no observations, no policy and
no intents, in a file that has all three.

Docs and comments only; `cargo fmt --check` is clean on both touched crates.
